correctness.rationale: The duad–syntheme incidence graph is cubic and bipartite; two disjoint duads lie in their unique completed matching, and three pairwise disjoint duads already comprise a single matching. These facts rule out cycles of lengths four and six. The independently computed distance profiles give layers 1,3,6,12,8 at every vertex. Cubicity, girth and bipartite parity give the stated radius-2 and radius-1 intersections with the distance-four shell; their maxima are 4 and 2. Thus even an unrestricted four-source tuple misses at least one vertex. Equality requires the second and third balls to hit 4 and 2 previously missed vertices and the singleton to add one more. For first duad 01, the distance-two second choice leaves the four crosses over its two labels, with two disjoint-pair completions; the distance-four second choice leaves one cross disjoint from each of the three others, with three completions. In either case there are two ways to place the last singleton. The automorphism listed in the frozen proof exchanges the two sides, and the stabilizer of a first duad is transitive on its eight antipodes. These facts explain counts 24+48 per source and nine per survivor. Independently enumerating all 27,000 first-three-source triples gives a minimum of two vertices missing and exactly 1,080 such triples. The two possible singleton extensions per minimizing triple exhaust all four-source maximizers; all 2,160 satisfy the six required distance constraints, with the exact advertised source–survivor and distance distributions. Five pairwise intersecting duads are pairwise at graph distance four, so the five-round construction is legal and its first ball covers. No four-round cover implies no shorter one because any shorter cover could be extended to an unrestricted four-tuple.
residual_risks: Enumeration is exhaustive for this labelled instance via the proved reduction, not a result on other cages or ignition conventions. value.rationale: This is a complete exact invariant at the critical pre-completion time on a canonical highly symmetric cage. It measures the gap between the relaxed coverage objective and genuine completion, then identifies the entire class of near-complete schedules, including their legality and survivor distribution. These are natural quantities independent of how they were computed and suitable as an exact benchmark; the structural two-case description explains more than the burning number or a sample count would.
residual_risks: A benchmark for the particular 30-vertex cage; no generalization to other graphs or spread rules is asserted.
